- Configurable logging/retention (30/90/365 days) and ability to forward logs to customer endpoints (Splunk/HTTP/SQS/Kinesis).

Hi Jane / Tom —

Following up with more detail ahead of our call and to answer the questions you raised: 

1) Retention and PII handling- Default retention windows are configurable per-deployment. Out of the box we provide configurable presets (30 / 90 / 365 days). We can scope a per-tenant policy for PII that enforces shorter retention and/or automatic redaction of specific fields before persistence. For Private deployments the default behavior is to not persist request/response payloads unless explicitly enabled — metadata and audit events are preserved.

2) Logging and SIEM integration- Audit logs (auth events, API call metadata, model selection, error traces) are written to customer-controlled S3 buckets or our managed store depending on deployment mode. For Private/VPC we typically push logs to a customer S3 or support a direct streaming connector (Kinesis, Kafka, or HTTPS webhook) to forward events to Splunk/Datadog in near real-time. Logs do not include full request/response payloads by default; payload logging must be explicitly enabled and is logged to a separate, opt-in stream (we can gate that with RBAC).

3) Network boundaries and egress controls- Private VPC options include:
  - Private ENIs + VPC endpoints so no public IPs are used for inference traffic.
  - Optional VPC peering or Transit Gateway for routing between AcmeHealth subnets and Redwood-managed subnets.
  - Egress control via customer-managed NAT/GW or our managed egress proxies; we can restrict allowed destinations to a whitelist (e.g., KMS endpoints, container registries).
  - For additional assurance, we can terminate external dependencies (model downloads, telemetry) inside customer network or use an approved mirror registry.

4) Data residency / artifacts- For Private deployments we run compute inside the customer VPC/region and can ensure model artifacts and logs remain in-region. Model cache eviction and any persisted artifacts are stored on customer provisioned volumes. If you require, we can sign an addendum to explicitly state no artifact egress without written approval.

5) On-prem / air-gapped support- We do offer an on-prem/offline deployment package for regulated workloads. It includes:
  - A deployment bundle (air-gapped installer), offline model bundle delivery, and procedures for certificate rotation and patching.
  - Documentation on operational cutover and a support engagement for the first 90 days.
  - Some advanced features (auto-scaling to managed pools) are limited in fully offline mode; we’ll scope which features are required.

6) KMS & key management- Customer-managed KMS is supported; keys are used for at-rest encryption of model cache and persistent stores. We can integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or customer HSMs where supported.

- Confirm which logs you want forwarded and the schema (we’ll provide a sample).
- If air-gapped is required, Rafael will scope the deployment effort and share an SOW estimate.

If helpful, I can also provide a brief sample log export and a sanitized example of our audit events prior to the call.
